newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks mixed in cautious late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks mixed in cautious late trade.

text.p: Taiwan shares turned mixed in late trade on Thursday after opening sharply higher, as brokers said investors were digesting the central bank's Wednesday call for extra caution in the red-hot stock market.
With 50 minutes left, the index was down 7.17 points or 0.08 percent at 8,648.65, well back from an opening high of 8,758.41.
Turnver was a brisk T$135 billion.
Constructions, cements and financials rose, but steels and electronics, the recent gainers, fell on profit-taking.
Brokers said investors nonetheless remained positive.

"Sentiment remains bullish despite the central bank warning, because most investors believe the central bank will not have strong moves to cool down the market other than moral persuasion or open market operations" to slightly tighten liquidity, said National Securities anlayst Alex Yang.
"As the economic recovery is still slow and the government's competitiveness has faced criticism, the government will not risk hitting the stock market to anger the public," Yang said.
Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung warned after the close on Wednesday that Taiwan's stock market turnover rate and price-earnings ratio were far higher than other countries'.
"Investors should be risk-conscious and be extra careful. What the central bank can do has already been done," Hsu said without elaboration.
The central bank said it would issue T$3 billion in three-month negotiable certificates of deposit on Thursday.
The bank has consistently denied that its repeated issuance of the short-term instruments in recent weeks intended to take some of the fire from the sizzling stock market.
Analysts suspect otherwise, saying persistently loose liquidity has been a key factor driving a huge stock rally that has pushed the share index 25 percent higher in 1997 alone.
